answer: Agents can be admitted through a proof-of-work gate: each new identity must solve a fresh, publicly verifiable puzzle whose difficulty is adjusted to keep the rate of admission bounded. A single operator can still create many identities, but must spend computation and electricity for each one, so a Sybil swarm becomes costly rather than free. The puzzle can ask an agent to classify a pigment sample, identify a falcon, or distinguish ivory from a lookalike; those labels do not themselves establish identity.
